bindings.name: AI_SEARCH
bindings.what: Retrieval and answer generation for Ask, on built-in storage with uploaded markdown rather than the crawler.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: It sits above classic search rather than replacing it, because the two fail on OPPOSITE inputs. Measured on the same corpus: classic found 2 things AI retrieval missed, all exact tokens, and AI retrieval found 3 that classic missed, all natural-language questions. Neither layer subsumes the other.

bindings.name: ASSETS
bindings.what: The static files under public/, served without a Worker invocation.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: The binding has exactly one method, fetch(), so a Worker can serve any path it is given and discover none of them. That is why the media rebuild reads a committed manifest: the one thing it cannot do for itself is find out which static files exist.

bindings.name: DB
bindings.what: SQLite at the edge. Holds every post, the tag graph, the derived search corpus, the media index and the llms.txt row.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: The media index lives here because R2 paginates in key order and promises nothing else. Sort by date, filter unused, search by name, count by type: each is a query, and building one over a key-ordered iterator means listing the whole bucket per request. A capability decision, not a scale one.

bindings.name: ASK_BUDGET
bindings.what: The per-IP burst limit and the site-wide daily ceiling for Ask, on the synchronous SQLite storage API.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: Both cheaper mechanisms were built first and both leaked. The GA ratelimit binding, configured at 5 per 60 seconds and attacked with 12 concurrent requests, refused 1, then 2, then 9, then 0 across four runs. A Durable Object using async storage.get then storage.put allowed 8 through a ceiling of 3, because a read and a write spanning an await is not atomic. The synchronous API allowed exactly 3, which is why the class is registered as new_sqlite_classes.

bindings.name: IMAGES
bindings.what: Thumbnail and content-width transforms, computed on request from the original. Nothing is written back.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: The BINDING and not the /cdn-cgi/image/ URL syntax, and that is forced rather than preferred: the URL interface answers 404 with Cloudflare error 1042 on this hostname, because transformations there require a zone and this site is served from workers.dev.

bindings.name: APP_KV
bindings.what: Better Auth sessions, and the Ask answer cache keyed by a SHA-256 of the normalised question.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: The cache sits in front of the daily ceiling rather than behind it, so a repeated question costs nothing and consumes no budget. The ordering is the design: a hit reaches no model.

bindings.name: dustinedwards-media-events
bindings.what: R2 event notifications from both buckets, consumed to derive the media index rows.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: The write path is a notification into a queue, never a dual write. The Worker writes only to R2 and the consumer re-derives the row from the object as it is now, never branching on what the message claimed, which is what makes replay and out-of-order delivery converge.

bindings.name: MEDIA
bindings.what: Uploaded originals, content-addressed as sha256(bytes) truncated plus the extension.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: Content addressing was decided on security, not tidiness. The old key was derivable from public information, so a draft's images were reachable by guessing a slug the sitemap publishes plus eight hex characters.

bindings.name: OG
bindings.what: Social cards, one per post, rebuilt by command.
bindings.whyLoadBearing: A second bucket exists because the two split on LIFECYCLE rather than on what the UI calls them. MEDIA is irreplaceable; OG is regenerable, so it is safe to empty and is deliberately outside the backup path.

notAdopted.name: Vectorize
notAdopted.reason: Rank fusion over two FTS5 indexes answers this corpus in about fifteen lines and no vectors. Zero-result queries are the cheapest content-gap signal the site has, and the only evidence that would justify reopening the question.

notAdopted.name: Images storage
notAdopted.reason: Transforms are used; storage is not. It bills in $5 increments per 100,000 stored images, for a library of dozens.

notAdopted.name: Soft delete and a trash prefix
notAdopted.reason: A team concern. The audience is one person, and R2 wins every conflict already, so a deleted row that should not have gone is restored by the next rebuild.

notAdopted.name: Media versioning
notAdopted.reason: Keys are content-addressed, so a changed image is a different key by construction. Versioning would be a second mechanism for something the addressing already does.

notAdopted.name: Single-flight on Ask
notAdopted.reason: Declined with the bound written into the route. Deduplicating identical questions does not lower the worst case: N addresses spend the same N units asking N DIFFERENT questions. The 200 per day ceiling is the real bound and it is exact.

notAdopted.name: Continuous integration
notAdopted.reason: Not a refusal so much as an accepted gap, recorded because it has already cost something: with no CI, any gate can be skipped indefinitely, and check:admin-ui was red and unrun for two sessions. The repair built instead was one command that runs every gate and derives the list, so nobody has to remember which ones a change touches.
